newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Monday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
Turnover fell to 2.559 billion yuan from 2.825 billion yuan last Friday with the 30-day contract the most actively traded.
Traders said trading was active due to lively trading on the domestic A share markets, which saw securities houses borrowing more money on the interbank market.
State-run banks were major net lenders, they said.
The China Securities newspaper said a central state debt depository set up earlier this year would soon begin trial operations.

Traders said the new operations would reduce trading turnover on China's state debt repurchase market and make trading on the interbank market more active. In the next few days, the interbank rates would move in a narrow range, they said.
